title: Workspace Heartbeat MCP Plugin v1
goal: Build and validate a minimal MCP heartbeat tool plus ChatGPT conversation-panel UI so long-running workspace-control tasks can publish natural-language progress through a real tool call into one continuously updating side panel.
acceptance_criteria: Expose a model-callable heartbeat_update tool whose user-facing progress content is natural prose rather than rigid structured headings.
Expose a read-only heartbeat_get tool that returns the latest heartbeat for the current ChatGPT conversation and optional task ID.
Use the anonymized openai/session tool-call metadata to isolate heartbeat state between ChatGPT conversations while retaining task_id as the domain identifier.
Advertise a ChatGPT thread conversation-panel entrypoint that displays one rolling heartbeat box beside the chat.
Update the panel in place by reading heartbeat_get without creating one inline widget per heartbeat_update call.
Assign monotonic per-session/task sequence numbers so stale panel refreshes cannot overwrite newer state.
Keep the MVP useful without UI through normal structuredContent/content tool results.
Keep v0.1 storage in memory and explicitly defer persistence, auth, deployment, history, and stronger cross-tool lease enforcement.
Provide focused deterministic unit tests for store sequencing, session isolation, latest-task lookup, and empty state.
Provide a local run/test/developer-mode handoff using the official MCP Inspector and an HTTPS development tunnel or deployment.
Do not mutate research-engine or any course/research repository as part of this plugin implementation.
constraints: Use current documented OpenAI/MCP Apps APIs and a ChatGPT thread entrypoint; do not depend on hidden client behavior.
Do not treat UI commentary/thought rendering as authoritative heartbeat delivery.
Do not expose private chain-of-thought; heartbeat_update carries concise operator-facing progress prose only.
Do not commit per-heartbeat runtime state to Git.
Do not introduce a database, OAuth flow, public cloud deployment, or event-streaming backend until the local/developer-mode MVP works.

Do not claim this MCP server can physically block unrelated GitHub or other external tool calls; the three-tool lease remains an executor contract unless operations are later proxied through a controllable orchestrator.
Keep all implementation inside workspace-control plugins/workspace-heartbeat/** plus this task capsule/handoff.

next_safe_action: With the Workspace heartbeat thread panel visibly open in normal Chat mode, invoke heartbeat_update once for the owning task and verify the panel changes from its idle state to the emitted natural-language message with sequence 1. Then invoke heartbeat_update a second time and verify the same panel updates in place to sequence 2. Treat model prose such as 'the panel is working' as non-evidence unless the user visibly observes the panel update. Successful MCP requests are not currently printed by server.js, so an empty MCP terminal is not evidence of no request; use the ngrok request log or add explicit request logging if transport proof is needed. Do not add persistence/auth/history/SSE before the update loop is proven.
notes: The user explicitly wants heartbeat delivery to be a tool call and the UI to be one updating formatted box, while heartbeat prose remains natural and conversational. Live evidence now proves the thread side panel renders in normal Chat mode. The first authorization attempt using 'Use once' produced an 'Unable to load conversation' error; retrying after refresh with 'Always allow' allowed the chat to continue. The research chat claimed the live heartbeat panel was working before the user had observed any panel; such model prose is not accepted as evidence. The MCP server currently logs startup/errors only, not successful requests, so an idle MCP terminal cannot prove that no request occurred. System Node v12.22.9 is unsupported for this implementation; Node 20 in a dedicated conda environment is the working runtime. tmux helpers heartbeat-up/heartbeat-status/heartbeat-console/heartbeat-down keep both MCP and ngrok alive across SSH disconnects.
